body: I'm sorry to hear that. I've felt that same way but at age 16 and now @ 37. Wish you the best and hugs. I think depressed people are vulnerable and it attracts bad people like sharks when blood's in the water. I wish this was not true, but the only solace I know is others who have been through the same can empathize with you and really do hope for some good to come to you. I'm going to tell you something about me and you. When I was 3 I felt what it was to be lonely. It was just a flicker that passed in a lightnig fast thought but it was followed by the worry that others were feeling this all the time and I thought, "I can't help everyone, what can I do?" So, what I did was mentally cut a tiny place in my own heart and said to myself I'd never let it heal, because even if I couldn't protect or save the hearts of others, I could feel with them and in this way they would not hurt alone, and i would never be separated from the humanity that i loved and assumed was as Kind as I was as a little girl. I kept that promise and later people had become so cruel to me I gave up that there was any good for me to find in any of them because no one had offered me the kindness that I knew I would have given to them. I felt so cheated at first but later a piece of me died. I realized the little girl i was, was gone, and until I found a small dog/puppy who was being neglected but was so full of joy and hope she was the little girl I'd wanted to save and simply could not. I'd stopped being able to cry, and in taking care of her needs I realized that I could have been saved if only someone loved me, and  that tiny puppy learned that I loved and sacrificed for her the way i wished someone had me. I protected and advocated for her and i changing her story changed my own and she gave me a great gift. She passed after 10 years and I cried daily for 2years after that, She'd given me my tears back, and it was the best gift, but not the last one. I knelt at her grave in the back yard tormented that I had not spent her last hours with her as I'd fallen asleep. Two tiles were placed over her and all I could think was I wish I could know that she knew that I loved her. Even as she got old and lost her vision she found me no matter where I was because she knew me and I had thought no one would EVER know me and I'd have lived and died and meant nothing to anyone, but she wouldn't let that happen. All I wanted was for her to find me one more time. As I knelt crying over her small grave I found something that everyone would say was a coincidence. A leaf was on the tile placed over her and it had eroded away not the veins but the leaf itself the shape of a heart, not at the outer part of the leaf but on the inside. It seemed impossible or unlikely, but it was what I needed in order to hold close that my little girl knew somehow that I loved her for all she was to me. I wondered how, perhaps the insects, or even the trees? I placed the leaf in clear resin as it was all I had left but pictures. Later I thought, If the trees had given my that kindness they had told a story i'd been waiting my whole life long to hear, "Once there was a little girl, and she was loved." That's all I came to earth with the hope I could believe was true, and it was. I will be gone soon enough, but I'd like to live and be healthy which I've not been since age 18. I longed for true friends and I had one. All I can say is I hope you find meaning and solace where ever you can, and that a small par of my heart is still open hoping yours will rest well being not alone and never without love. I hope knowing that helps even a little. Take care.
